**How Abbott manages foreign currency exposure (FY2024, year ended Dec 31, 2024)**

Abbott is heavily exposed to currency movements: sales outside the U.S. were about 61% of 2024 net sales (Item 1A, chunk 65600). Management describes a layered hedging program, disclosed in Item 7A (chunk 166400) and Note 12 (chunks 235200–240000):

1. **Cash flow hedges of anticipated intercompany purchases** by foreign subsidiaries whose functional currency is not the U.S. dollar. Gross notional was **$7.0 billion at Dec 31, 2024 vs. $7.3 billion at Dec 31, 2023** (down ~4.1%, calculated). These are marked to market through Accumulated OCI, with gains/losses reclassified into Cost of products sold when the products are sold, generally within 12–18 months; 2024 contracts mature in 2025 or 2026.
2. **Economic (non-designated) hedges of balance-sheet exposures** — foreign-currency intercompany loans, intercompany/third-party trade payables and receivables. Gross notional rose to **$16.2 billion at Dec 31, 2024 from $13.8 billion at Dec 31, 2023** (up ~17.4%, calculated), maturing within 13 months. Gains/losses run through income and are generally offset by the re-measurement of the hedged item. Exposures are primarily the U.S. dollar and European currencies.
3. **Net investment hedge**: a yen-denominated 5-year term loan of about **$583 million at Dec 31, 2024 vs. $419 million at Dec 31, 2023** (up ~39%, calculated; the increase reflects $201 million of net incremental borrowing plus FX), designated against the net investment in certain foreign subsidiaries, with changes in Accumulated OCI.

**Did the exposure change recently?** Yes, in both directions. Total forward notional (cash flow plus economic hedges) increased from roughly $21.1 billion to $23.2 billion year over year, driven mainly by the ~$2.4 billion increase in balance-sheet hedging, while cash-flow hedge notional slipped slightly. The realized drag also eased: FX reduced total international sales by **4.2% and total sales by 2.6% in 2024**, versus **3.5% and 2.0%** in 2023 (MD&A, chunk 113600) — i.e., a larger negative translation effect in 2024 despite the hedging. Hedge results were volatile: cash flow hedges recognized a **$347 million gain in OCI in 2024 versus a $22 million loss in 2023**, with $103 million reclassified to income in 2024 versus $187 million in 2023 (chunk 240000).

**Caveats:** These are notional amounts, not net exposure or fair value; the filing does not quantify a single net FX exposure figure. Abbott explicitly states it "cannot predict with any certainty changes in foreign currency exchange rates or its ability to mitigate these risks" (chunk 62400). Only the FY2024 10-K is available in the bundled data, so the 2023 comparatives come from that filing rather than a separate 2023 report.
